name: problem_10_5
docstring:
Problem 10.5 (first part). Let $\mathbb{K}$ be a real number field. Then, for any
$\varepsilon > 0$, there exists a lacunary sequence $(t_n)_{n \ge 1}$ of positive numbers
in $\mathbb{K}$ such that
$$\limsup_{n \to \infty} \{\xi t_n\} \ge 1 - \varepsilon,$$
for any real number $\xi$ not in $\mathbb{K}$.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem problem_10_5 (K : IntermediateField ℚ ℝ) [FiniteDimensional ℚ K]
    {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ t : ℕ → K, (∀ n, 0 < (t n : ℝ)) ∧
      IsLacunaryReal (fun k => (t k : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ ξ : ℝ, ξ ∉ K →
        (1 - ε) ≤ limsup (fun n => Int.fract (ξ * (t n : ℝ))) atTop := by
  sorry

name: problem_10_5_moreover
docstring:
Problem 10.5 ("moreover" clause). With the same hypotheses as `problem_10_5`, the
sequence $(t_n)$ can be chosen so that, for any real $\xi$ not in $\mathbb{K}$, each
subinterval of $[0, 1]$ of length $\varepsilon$ contains a limit point of the sequence
$(\{\xi t_n\})_{n \ge 1}$. This is strictly stronger than `problem_10_5`: the limsup
bound is the special case at the subinterval $[1 - \varepsilon, 1]$.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem problem_10_5_moreover (K : IntermediateField ℚ ℝ) [FiniteDimensional ℚ K]
    {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ t : ℕ → K, (∀ n, 0 < (t n : ℝ)) ∧
      IsLacunaryReal (fun k => (t k : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ ξ : ℝ, ξ ∉ K → ∀ a, a ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) (1 - ε) →
        ∃ y ∈ Set.Icc a (a + ε),
          MapClusterPt y atTop (fun n => Int.fract (ξ * (t n : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

name: problem_10_6_variant_1
docstring:
Problem 10.6. Find a very rapidly increasing sequence $(m_n)_{n \ge 1}$ of positive
integers such that $(\{\xi m_n\})_{n \ge 1}$ is dense modulo one for every irrational
number $\xi$. Note: Furstenberg's $2^m3^n$ is sublacunary but requires two parameters.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem problem_10_6_variant_1 :
    ∃ m : ℕ → ℕ,
    StrictMono m ∧
    IsGenuinelySublacunary m ∧
    ∀ ξ : ℝ, Irrational ξ →
      Dense (Set.range fun n => (↑(ξ * m n) : AddCircle (1 : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

name: problem_10_6_variant_2
docstring: Problem 10.6, intermediate-growth variant.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem problem_10_6_variant_2 :
    ∃ m : ℕ → ℕ,
    StrictMono m ∧
    (∃ α : ℝ, 0 < α ∧ α < 1 ∧ HasIntermediateGrowth α m) ∧
    ∀ ξ : ℝ, Irrational ξ →
      Dense (Set.range fun n => (↑(ξ * m n) : AddCircle (1 : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

name: problem_10_7
docstring:
Problem 10.7. Let $\varepsilon$ be a positive real number. Are there arbitrarily
large real numbers $\alpha$ such that $\alpha$ is not a Pisot number and all the
fractional parts $\{\alpha^n\}$, $n \ge 1$, are lying in an interval of length
$\varepsilon / \alpha$? [Bug12b]
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem problem_10_7 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ M : ℝ, ∃ α : ℝ, M < α ∧ ¬ IsPisot α ∧
      ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → Int.fract (α ^ n) ∈ Set.Icc c (c + ε / α) := by
  sorry

name: problem_10_8
docstring:
Problem 10.8 ($p$-adic Littlewood conjecture). For every real number $\xi$ and
every prime number $p$,
$$\inf_{q \ge 1} q \cdot \lVert q \xi \rVert \cdot |q|_p = 0,$$
where $\lVert \cdot \rVert$ denotes the distance to the nearest integer and
$|\cdot|_p$ denotes the $p$-adic absolute value. Posed by de Mathan and
Teulié [dMT04].
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem problem_10_8 (ξ : ℝ) (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) :
    sInf {x : ℝ | ∃ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q ∧
      x = q * padicNorm p q * distToNearestInt (q * ξ)} = 0 := by
  sorry

name: beaver_math_olympiad_problem_1
docstring:
[BMO#1](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/Beaver_Math_Olympiad#1._1RB1RE_1LC0RA_0RD1LB_---1RC_1LF1RE_0LB0LE_(bbch))

Let $(a_n)_{n \ge 1}$ and $(b_n)_{n \ge 1}$ be two sequences such that $(a_1, b_1) = (1, 2)$ and

$$(a_{n+1}, b_{n+1}) = \begin{cases}
(a_n-b_n, 4b_n+2) & \text{if }a_n \ge b_n \\
(2a_n+1, b_n-a_n) & \text{if }a_n < b_n
\end{cases}$$

for all positive integers $n$. Does there exist a positive integer $i$ such that $a_i = b_i$?

The first 10 values of $(a_n, b_n)$ are $(1, 2), (3, 1), (2, 6), (5, 4), (1, 18), (3, 17),
(7, 14), (15, 7), (8, 30), (17, 22)$.

[BMO#1](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/Beaver_Math_Olympiad#1._1RB1RE_1LC0RA_0RD1LB_---1RC_1LF1RE_0LB0LE_(bbch)) is equivalent to asking whether the 6-state Turing machine
[`1RB1RE_1LC0RA_0RD1LB_---1RC_1LF1RE_0LB0LE`](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/1RB1RE_1LC0RA_0RD1LB_---1RC_1LF1RE_0LB0LE) halts or not.

There is presently no consensus on whether the machine halts or not, hence the problem is formulated
using `answer(sorry) ↔`.

The machine was discovered by [bbchallenge.org](bbchallenge.org) contributor Jason Yuen on
June 25th 2024.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5 11 68]
theorem beaver_math_olympiad_problem_1 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (a : ℕ → ℕ) (b : ℕ → ℕ)
    (a_ini : a 0 = 1)
    (a_rec : ∀ n, a (n + 1) = if b n ≤ a n then a n - b n else 2 * a n + 1)
    (b_ini : b 0 = 2)
    (b_rec : ∀ n, b (n + 1) = if b n ≤ a n then 4 * b n + 2 else b n - a n),
    ∃ i, a i = b i := by
  sorry

name: beaver_math_olympiad_problem_2_antihydra
docstring:
[BMO#2](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/Beaver_Math_Olympiad#2._Hydra_and_Antihydra)

Antihydra is a sequence starting at 8, and iterating the function
$$H(n) = \left\lfloor \frac {3n}2 \right\rfloor.$$
The conjecture states that the cumulative number of odd values in this sequence
is never more than twice the cumulative number of even values. It is a relatively new open problem
with, so it might be solvable, although seems quite hard because of its Collatz-like flavor.
The underlying Collatz-like map has been studied independently in the past,
see doi:[10.1017/S0017089508004655](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0017089508004655) (Corollary 4).

It is equivalent to non-termination of the [`1RB1RA_0LC1LE_1LD1LC_1LA0LB_1LF1RE_---0RA`](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/Antihydra) 6-state Turing machine (from all-0 tape). Note that the conjecture
that the machine does not halt is based on [a probabilistic argument](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/Antihydra#Trajectory).

This machine and its mathematical reformulations were found by [bbchallenge.org](bbchallenge.org)
contributors mxdys and Rachel Hunter on June 28th 2024.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5 11 68]
theorem beaver_math_olympiad_problem_2_antihydra
    (a : ℕ → ℕ) (b : ℕ → ℤ)
    (a_ini : a 0 = 8)
    (a_rec : ∀ n, a (n + 1) = (3 * a n) / 2)
    (b_ini : b 0 = 0)
    (b_rec : ∀ n, b (n + 1) = if a n % 2 = 0 then b n + 2 else b n - 1) :
    ∀ n, b n ≥ 0 := by
  sorry

name: beaver_math_olympiad_problem_2_antihydra.variants.set
docstring:
[BMO#2](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/Beaver_Math_Olympiad#2._Hydra_and_Antihydra) formulation variant

Alternative statement of beaver_math_olympiad_problem_2_antihydra
using set size comparison instead of a recurrent sequence b.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5 11 68]
theorem beaver_math_olympiad_problem_2_antihydra.variants.set
    (a : ℕ → ℕ) (a_ini : a 0 = 8)
    (a_rec : ∀ n, a (n + 1) = (3 * a n) / 2) (n : ℕ) :
    ((Finset.Ico 0 n).filter fun x ↦ Odd (a x)).card ≤
      2 * ((Finset.Ico 0 n).filter fun x ↦ Even (a x)).card := by
  sorry

name: beaver_math_olympiad_problem_5
docstring:
[BMO#5](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/Beaver_Math_Olympiad#5._1RB0LD_1LC0RA_1RA1LB_1LA1LE_1RF0LC_---0RE_(bbch))

Let $(a_n)_{n \ge 1}$ and $(b_n)_{n \ge 1}$ be two sequences such that $(a_1, b_1) = (0, 5)$ and

$$(a_{n+1}, b_{n+1}) = \begin{cases}
(a_n+1, b_n-f(a_n)) & \text{if } b_n \ge f(a_n) \\
(a_n, 3b_n+a_n+5) & \text{if } b_n < f(a_n)
\end{cases}$$

where $f(x)=10\cdot 2^x-1$ for all non-negative integers $x$.

Does there exist a positive integer $i$ such that $b_i = f(a_i)-1$?

[BMO#5](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/Beaver_Math_Olympiad#5._1RB0LD_1LC0RA_1RA1LB_1LA1LE_1RF0LC_---0RE_(bbch)) is equivalent to asking whether the 6-state Turing machine
[`1RB0LD_1LC0RA_1RA1LB_1LA1LE_1RF0LC_---0RE`](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/1RB0LD_1LC0RA_1RA1LB_1LA1LE_1RF0LC_---0RE) halts or not.

There is presently no consensus on whether the machine halts or not, hence the problem is formulated
using `answer(sorry) ↔`.

The machine was discovered by [bbchallenge.org](bbchallenge.org) contributor mxdys
on August 7th 2024.

The correspondence between the machine's halting problem and the below reformulation has been proven
in [Rocq](https://github.com/ccz181078/busycoq/blob/BB6/verify/1RB0LD_1LC0RA_1RA1LB_1LA1LE_1RF0LC_---0RE.v).
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5 11 68]
theorem beaver_math_olympiad_problem_5 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (a b f : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ᵉ (hf : f = fun x ↦ 10 * 2 ^ x - 1)
    (a_ini : a 0 = 0) (b_ini : b 0 = 5)
    (a_rec : ∀ n, a (n + 1) = if f (a n) ≤ b n then a n + 1 else a n)
    (b_rec : ∀ n, b (n+1) = if f (a n) ≤ b n then b n - f (a n) else 3 * b n + a n + 5),
    ∃ i, b i = f (a i) - 1 := by
  sorry

name: beaver_math_olympiad_problem_8
docstring:
[BMO#8](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/Beaver_Math_Olympiad#8._1RB0LD_0RC1RB_0RD0RA_1LE0RD_1LF---_0LA1LA_(bbch))

Let $(a_n)_{n \ge 1}$ and $(b_n)_{n \ge 1}$ be two sequences such that $(a_1, b_1) = (10, 12)$ and

$$(a_{n+1}, b_{n+1}) = \begin{cases}
(a_n - \lfloor b_n/2 \rfloor - 3, 3 \lfloor (b_n+1)/2 \rfloor + 6) & \text{if } a_n > \lfloor b_n/2 \rfloor \\
(3 a_n + 5, b_n - 2 a_n) & \text{if } a_n \le \lfloor b_n/2 \rfloor
\end{cases}$$

for all positive integers $n$.  Does there exist a positive integer $i$ such that
$a_i = \lfloor b_i/2 \rfloor + 1$?

[BMO#8](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/Beaver_Math_Olympiad#8._1RB0LD_0RC1RB_0RD0RA_1LE0RD_1LF---_0LA1LA_(bbch)) is equivalent to asking whether the 6-state Turing machine
[`1RB0LD_0RC1RB_0RD0RA_1LE0RD_1LF---_0LA1LA`](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/1RB0LD_0RC1RB_0RD0RA_1LE0RD_1LF---_0LA1LA) halts or not.

There is presently no consensus on whether the machine halts or not, hence the problem is formulated
using `answer(sorry) ↔`.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5 11 68]
theorem beaver_math_olympiad_problem_8 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ᵉ (a : ℕ → ℕ) (b : ℕ → ℕ)
    (a_ini : a 0 = 10)
    (a_rec : ∀ n, a (n + 1) =
      if b n / 2 < a n then a n - b n / 2 - 3 else 3 * a n + 5)
    (b_ini : b 0 = 12)
    (b_rec : ∀ n, b (n + 1) =
      if b n / 2 < a n then 3 * ((b n + 1) / 2) + 6 else b n - 2 * a n),
    ∃ i, a i = b i / 2 + 1 := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1
docstring:
If $A\subseteq\{1, ..., N\}$ with $|A| = n$ is such that the subset sums $\sum_{a\in S}a$ are
distinct for all $S\subseteq A$ then
$$
  N \gg 2 ^ n.
$$
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_1 : ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (N : ℕ) (A : Finset ℕ) (_ : IsSumDistinctSet A N),
    N ≠ 0 → C * 2 ^ A.card < N := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1.variants.real
docstring:
A generalisation of the problem to sets $A \subseteq (0, N]$ of real numbers, such that the subset
sums all differ by at least $1$ is proposed in [Er73] and [ErGr80].

[Er73] Erdős, P., _Problems and results on combinatorial number theory_. A survey of combinatorial theory (Proc. Internat. Sympos., Colorado State Univ., Fort Collins, Colo., 1971) (1973), 117-138.

[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., _Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory_. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_1.variants.real : ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (N : ℕ) (A : Finset ℝ)
    (_ : IsSumDistinctRealSet A N), N ≠ 0 → C * 2 ^ A.card < N := by
  sorry

name: erdos_10
docstring:
Is there some $k$ such that every integer is the sum of a prime and at most $k$
powers of $2$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_10 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ k, sumPrimeAndTwoPows k = Set.univ \ {0, 1} := by
  sorry

name: erdos_10.variants.granville_soundararajan_odd
docstring:
Granville and Soundararajan [GrSo98] have conjectured that at most $3$
powers of $2$ suffice for all odd integers, and hence at most $4$ powers of $2$
suffice for all even integers.

Ref: Granville, A. and Soundararajan, K., _A Binary Additive Problem of Erdős and the Order of $2$ mod $p^2$_
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_10.variants.granville_soundararajan_odd :
    {n : ℕ | Odd n ∧ 1 < n} ⊆ sumPrimeAndTwoPows 3 ∧
      {n : ℕ | Even n ∧ n ≠ 0} ⊆ sumPrimeAndTwoPows 4 := by
  sorry

name: erdos_10.variants.grechuk
docstring:
Bogdan Grechuk has observed that $1117175146$ is not the sum of a prime and at most $3$
powers of $2$, and pointed out that parity considerations, coupled with the fact that there
are many integers not the sum of a prime and $2$ powers of $2$ suggest that there exist
infinitely many even integers which are not the sum of a prime and at most $3$ powers of $2$).
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_10.variants.grechuk :
    Set.Infinite <| {n : ℕ | Even n} \ sumPrimeAndTwoPows 3 := by
  sorry

name: erdos_100
docstring: Is the diameter of $A$ at least $Cn$ for some constant $C > 0$?

@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_100 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ A : Finset ℝ²,
      A.card = n →
      DistancesSeparated A →
      diam (A : Set ℝ²) > C * n := by
  sorry

name: erdos_100.variants.strong
docstring: Stronger conjecture: diameter $\geq n - 1$ for sufficiently large $n$.

@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_100.variants.strong :
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ A : Finset ℝ²,
      A.card = n →
      DistancesSeparated A →
      diam (A : Set ℝ²) ≥ n - 1 := by

name: erdos_1002
docstring:
For any $0<\alpha<1$, let $f(\alpha,n)=\frac{1}{\log n}\sum_{1\leq k\leq n}(\tfrac{1}{2}-
\{ \alpha k\})$. Does $f(\alpha,n)$ have an asymptotic distribution function?

In other words, is there a non-decreasing function $g$ such that $g(-\infty)=0$, $g(\infty)=1$,
and $\lim_{n\to \infty}\lvert \{ \alpha\in (0,1): f(\alpha,n)\leq c\}\rvert=g(c)$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1002 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ g : ℝ → ℝ, Monotone g ∧
      Tendsto g atBot (𝓝 0) ∧
      Tendsto g atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
      letI f :=  fun (α : ℝ) (n : ℕ) ↦
        (1 / log n) * ∑ k ∈ Icc (1 : ℕ) n, (1 / 2 - Int.fract (α * k))
      ∀ c : ℝ, Tendsto (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (volume { α | α ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧ f α n ≤ c }).toReal)
        atTop (𝓝 (g c)) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1003
docstring:
Are there infinitely many solutions to $\phi(n) = \phi(n+1)$, where $\phi$ is the Euler totient
function?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1003 : answer(sorry) ↔ Set.Infinite {n | φ n = φ (n + 1)} := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1003.variants.Icc
docstring:
Erdős [Er85e] says that, presumably, for every $k \geq 1$ the equation
$$\phi(n) = \phi(n+1) = \cdots = \phi (n+k)$$ has infinitely many solutions.

[Er85e] Erdős, P., _Some problems and results in number theory_. Number theory and combinatorics. Japan 1984 (Tokyo, Okayama and Kyoto, 1984) (1985), 65-87.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1003.variants.Icc :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 1, {n | ∀ i ∈ Set.Icc 1 k, φ n = φ (n + i)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1004
docstring:
For any fixed c > 0, if x is sufficiently large then there exists n ≤ x such that
the values of φ(n+k) are all distinct for 1 ≤ k ≤ (log x)^c.
This is an open problem.
statement:

theorem erdos_1004 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x in atTop, ∃ n ≤ x,
      IsDistinctTotientRun n ⌊(Real.log (x : ℝ)) ^ c⌋₊ := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1038.parts.i
docstring:
What is the infimum of `|{x ∈ ℝ : |f x| < 1}|` over all nonconstant monic polynomials `f` such
that all of its roots are real and contained in `[-1,1]`?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 28]
theorem erdos_1038.parts.i (n : ℕ) : answer(sorry) =
    ⨅ f : {f : Polynomial ℝ // f.Monic ∧ f ≠ 1 ∧
    (f.roots.filter fun x => x ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1).card = f.natDegree},
    volume {x | |f.1.eval x| < 1} := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1041
docstring:
Let
$$ f(z) = \prod_{i=1}^{n} (z - z_i) \in \mathbb{C}[x] $$
with $|z_i| < 1$ for all $i$.

Conjecture: Must there always exist a path of length less than 2 in
$$ \{ z \in \mathbb{C} \mid |f(z)| < 1 \} $$
which connects two of the roots of $f$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 32]
theorem erdos_1041 :
    ∃ (z₁ z₂ : ℂ) (h : ({z₁, z₂} : Multiset ℂ) ≤ f.roots) (γ : Path z₁ z₂),
      Set.range γ ⊆ { z : ℂ | ‖f.eval z‖ < 1 } ∧ length (Set.range γ) < 2 := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1049
docstring:
Let $t>1$ be a rational number. Is
$\sum_{n=1}^\infty\frac{1}{t^n-1}=\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{\tau(n)}{t^n}$ irrational, where
$\tau(n)$ counts the divisors of $n$?

A conjecture of Chowla.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1049 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ t : ℚ, t > 1 → Irrational (∑' n : ℕ+, 1 / ((t : ℝ) ^ (n : ℕ) - 1)) := by
  sorry

docstring: Are there only finitely many unitary perfect numbers?

name: erdos_1054.parts.i
docstring:
Let $f(n)$ be the minimal integer $m$ such that $n$ is the sum of the $k$ smallest divisors
of $m$ for some $k\geq 1$. Is it true that $f(n)=o(n)$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1054.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ (fun n ↦ (f n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1054.parts.ii
docstring:
Let $f(n)$ be the minimal integer $m$ such that $n$ is the sum of the $k$ smallest divisors
of $m$ for some $k\geq 1$. Is it true that $f(n)=o(n)$ for almost all $n$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1054.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (A : Set ℕ), A.HasDensity 1 ∧
    (fun (n : A) ↦ (f ↑n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1054.parts.iii
docstring:
Let $f(n)$ be the minimal integer $m$ such that $n$ is the sum of the $k$ smallest divisors
of $m$ for some $k\geq 1$. Is it true that $\limsup f(n)/n=\infty$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1054.parts.iii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (A : Set ℕ), A.HasDensity 1 ∧
    atTop.limsup (fun n ↦ (f n : EReal) / n) = ⊤ := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1055
docstring:
A prime $p$ is in class $1$ if the only prime divisors of $p+1$ are
$2$ or $3$. In general, a prime $p$ is in class $r$ if every prime factor
of $p+1$ is in some class $\leq r-1$, with equality for at least one prime factor.
Are there infinitely many primes in each class?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1055 (r) : {p | p.Prime ∧ IsOfClass r p}.Infinite := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1055.variants.erdos_limit
docstring:
A prime $p$ is in class $1$ if the only prime divisors of $p+1$ are
$2$ or $3$. In general, a prime $p$ is in class $r$ if every prime factor
of $p+1$ is in some class $\leq r-1$, with equality for at least one prime factor.
If $p_r$ is the least prime in class $r$, then how does $p_r^{1/r}$ behave?
Erdos conjectured that this tends to infinity.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1055.variants.erdos_limit :
    Filter.atTop.Tendsto (fun r ↦ (p r : ℝ) ^ (1 / r : ℝ)) Filter.atTop := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1055.variants.selfridge_limit
docstring:
A prime $p$ is in class $1$ if the only prime divisors of $p+1$ are
$2$ or $3$. In general, a prime $p$ is in class $r$ if every prime factor
of $p+1$ is in some class $\leq r-1$, with equality for at least one prime factor.
If $p_r$ is the least prime in class $r$, then how does $p_r^{1/r}$ behave?
Selfridge conjectured that this is bounded.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1055.variants.selfridge_limit :
    ∃ M, ∀ r, (p r : ℝ) ^ (1 / r : ℝ) ≤ M := by
  sorry

-- TODO(Paul-Lez): formalize the rest of the problems on the page.

name: erdos_1056
docstring:
Let $k ≥ 2$. Does there exist a prime $p$ and consecutive intervals $I_0,\dots,I_k$
such that $\prod\limits_{n{\in}I_i}n \equiv 1 \mod n$ for all $1 \le i \le k$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1056 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ k ≥ 2, ∃ (p : ℕ) (_ : p.Prime) (boundaries : Fin (k + 1) → ℕ) (_ : StrictMono boundaries),
    AllModProdEqualsOne p boundaries := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1056.variants.noll_simmons
docstring:
Noll and Simmons asked, more generally, whether there are solutions to
$q_1! \equiv \dots \equiv q_k! \mod p$ for arbitrarily large $k$ (with $q_1 < \dots < q_k$).
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1056.variants.noll_simmons :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ k in Filter.atTop,
    ∃ (p : ℕ) (_ : p.Prime) (Q : Fin k → ℕ) (_ : StrictMono Q) (_ : ∀ i, Q i < p),
    ∀ i j : Fin k, (Q i)! ≡ (Q j)! [MOD p] := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1057
docstring:
Is it true that $C(x)=x^{1-o(1)}$?

This is discussed in problem A13 of Guy's collection [Gu04].
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1057 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ Tendsto (fun x ↦ Real.log (carmichaelCounting x) / Real.log x) atTop (𝓝 1) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1057.variants.pomerance
docstring:
Pomerance [Po89] gave a heuristic suggesting that this is the true order of growth, and in fact
$C(x)= x \exp\left(-(1+o(1))\frac{\log x\log\log\log x}{\log\log x}\right)$.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1057.variants.pomerance :
    answer(sorry) ↔ Tendsto (fun x ↦
      -(Real.log (carmichaelCounting x / x) * Real.log (Real.log x)) /
      (Real.log x * Real.log (Real.log (Real.log x)))) atTop (𝓝 1) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1059
docstring: Are there infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p - k!$ is composite for each $k$ such that $1 ≤ k! < p$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1059 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ Set.Infinite {p | p.Prime ∧ AllFactorialSubtractionsComposite p} := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1060.parts.i
docstring:
The conjecture is about the function $f(n)$ which counts the number of solutions to
$k\sigma(k)=n$, where $\sigma(k)$ is the sum of divisors of $k$. The first bound is that $f(n)$ grows slower
than any power of $n^(\frac{1}{\log\log n})$. The second bound is that $f(n)$ is at most a power of
$\log n$.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1060.parts.i :
    ∃ h : ℕ → ℝ,
      h =o[atTop] (fun n ↦ 1 / log (log n)) ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, #{k ≤ n | k * σ 1 k = n} ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ h n := by sorry

name: erdos_1060.parts.ii
docstring: Part (ii) of Erdős Problem 1060: bound on the number of $k \le n$ with $k \sigma_1(k) = n$.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1060.parts.ii :
    ∃ (C : ℝ), (fun n ↦ (#{k ≤ n | k * σ 1 k = n} : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      (fun n ↦ log n ^ C) := by sorry

name: erdos_1061
docstring:
How many (ordered) solutions are there to `σ(a) + σ(b) = σ(a + b)` with `a + b ≤ x`?
Is it true that this number is asymptotic to `c * x` for some constant `c > 0`?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1061 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ S ~[atTop] (fun x : ℝ ↦ c * x) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1062.parts.ii
docstring:
Erdős asked whether the limiting density `f n / n` exists and, if so, whether it is
irrational.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1062.parts.ii :
    (∃ l, Tendsto (fun n => (f n : ℝ) / n) atTop (𝓝 l) ∧ Irrational l) ↔ answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1063.better_upper
docstring: Estimate $n_k$ by finding a better upper bound.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1063.better_upper :
    let upper_bound : ℕ → ℝ := answer(sorry)
    (fun k => (n k : ℝ)) =O[atTop] upper_bound ∧
    upper_bound =o[atTop] fun k =>
      (k : ℝ) * ((Finset.Icc 1 (k - 1)).lcm (fun n : ℕ => n) : ℝ) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1065.parts.i
docstring:
Are there infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p = 2^k * q + 1$
for some prime $q$ and $k ≥ 0$?

This is mentioned as B46
in [Unsolved Problems in Number Theory](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-387-26677-0)
by *Richard K. Guy*
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1065.parts.i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ Set.Infinite {p | ∃ q k, p.Prime ∧ q.Prime ∧ p = 2^k * q + 1} := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1065.parts.ii
docstring:
Are there infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p = 2^k 3^l q + 1$
for some prime $q$ and $k ≥ 0$, $l ≥ 0$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1065.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    Set.Infinite {p | ∃ q k l, p.Prime ∧ q.Prime ∧ p = 2^k * 3^l * q + 1} := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1068
docstring:
Does every graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ contain a countable subgraph which is
infinitely connected?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1068 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_  1 →
      ∃ s : Set V, s.Countable ∧ InfinitelyConnected (G.induce s) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_107
docstring:
Let $f(n)$ be minimal such that any $f(n)$ points in $ℝ^2$, no three on a line,
contain $n$ points which form the vertices of a convex $n$-gon.
Prove that $f(n) = 2^{n-2} + 1$.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_107 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ n ≥ 3, f n = 2^(n - 2) + 1 := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1072.parts.i
docstring: Is it true that there are infinitely many $p$ for which $f(p) = p − 1$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1072.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ Set.Infinite {p | p.Prime ∧ f p = p - 1} := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1072.parts.ii
docstring: Is it true that $f(p)/p \to 0$ for $p \to \infty$ in a density 1 subset of the primes?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1072.parts.ii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (P : Set ℕ), P ⊆ {p | p.Prime} ∧ P.HasDensity 1 {p | p.Prime} ∧
      Tendsto (fun p => (f p / p : ℝ)) (atTop ⊓ principal P) (𝓝 0) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1072.variants.littleo
docstring:
Erdős, Hardy, and Subbarao [HaSu02], believed that the number of $p \le x$ for which $f(p)=p−1$
is $o(x/\log x)$.

[HaSu02] Hardy, G. E. and Subbarao, M. V., _A modified problem of Pillai and some related questions._
Amer. Math. Monthly (2002), 554--559.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1072.variants.littleo :
    (fun x ↦ (({p | p.Prime ∧ f p = p - 1} ∩ Icc 0 x).ncard : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      (fun x ↦ x / Real.log x) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1073
docstring: Is it true that $A(x) \le x^{o(1)}$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1073 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ), o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧ ∀ x, A x ≤ x ^ (o x) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1074.parts.i
docstring:
Let $S$ be the set of all $m\geq 1$ such that there exists a prime $p\not\equiv 1\pmod{m}$ such
that $m! + 1 \equiv 0\pmod{p}$. Does
$$
  \lim\frac{|S\cap[1, x]|}{x}
$$
exist?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1074.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c, EHSNumbers.HasDensity c := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1074.parts.ii
docstring:
Let $S$ be the set of all $m\geq 1$ such that there exists a prime $p\not\equiv 1\pmod{m}$ such
that $m! + 1 \equiv 0\pmod{p}$. What is
$$
  \lim\frac{|S\cap[1, x]|}{x}?
$$
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1074.parts.ii : EHSNumbers.HasDensity answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1074.parts.iii
docstring:
Similarly, if $P$ is the set of all primes $p$ such that there exists an $m$ with
$p\not\equiv 1\pmod{m}$ such that $m! + 1 \equiv 0\pmod{p}$, then does
$$
  \lim\frac{|P\cap[1, x]|}{\pi(x)}
$$
exist?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1074.parts.iii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c, PillaiPrimes.HasDensity c {p | p.Prime} := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1074.parts.iv
docstring:
Similarly, if $P$ is the set of all primes $p$ such that there exists an $m$ with
$p\not\equiv 1\pmod{m}$ such that $m! + 1 \equiv 0\pmod{p}$, then what is
$$
  \lim\frac{|P\cap[1, x]|}{\pi(x)}?
$$
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1074.parts.iv :
    PillaiPrimes.HasDensity answer(sorry) {p | p.Prime} := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1074.variants.EHSNumbers_one_half
docstring:
Regarding the first question, Hardy and Subbarao computed all EHS numbers up to $2^{10}$, and
write "...if this trend conditions we expect [the limit] to be around 0.5, if it exists."
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1074.variants.EHSNumbers_one_half : EHSNumbers.HasDensity (1 / 2) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_108
docstring:
For every r ≥ 4 and k ≥ 2 is there some finite f(k,r) such that every graph of chromatic number ≥ f(k,r)
contains a subgraph of girth ≥ r and chromatic number ≥ k?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_108 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ r ≥ 4, ∀ k ≥ (2 : ℕ), ∃ (f : ℕ),
    ∀ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V) (_ : Nonempty V)
      (hchro : f ≤ SimpleGraph.chromaticNumber G),
    ∃ (H : G.Subgraph), (SimpleGraph.girth H.coe ≥ r) ∧
    (SimpleGraph.chromaticNumber H.coe ≥ k) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1082.parts.i
docstring:
Let $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of $n$ points with no three on a line.
Does $A$ determine at least $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ distinct distances?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 51]
theorem erdos_1082.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (A : Finset ℝ²) (hA_n3c : NonTrilinear (A : Set ℝ²)),
    A.card / 2 ≤ distinctDistances A:= by
  sorry

name: erdos_1084.variants.triangular_optimal_d2
docstring:
Erdős conjectured that the triangular lattice is best possible in 2D, in particular that
$f_2(3n^2 + 3n + 1) < 9n^2 + 3n$.

Note: in [Er75f] is read $9n^2 + 6n$, but this seems to be a typo.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_1084.variants.triangular_optimal_d2 : f 2 (3 * n ^ 2 + 3 * n + 1) = 9 * n ^ 2 + 3 * n := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1085.variants.upper_d3
docstring: Is the $n^{4/3}\log\log n$ lower bound in 3D also an upper bound?.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_1085.variants.upper_d3 : answer(sorry) ↔
    (fun n ↦ (f 3 n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (4/3 : ℝ) * log (log n)) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1093.parts.i
docstring: Are there infinitely many binomial coefficients with deficiency 1?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1093.parts.i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ {x : ℕ × ℕ | let k := x.1; let n := x.2; 2 * k ≤ n ∧ deficiency n k = 1 ∧
      ∀ p, p.Prime → (p ∣ choose n k) → k < p}.Infinite := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1093.parts.ii
docstring: Are there only finitely many binomial coefficients with deficiency > 1?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1093.parts.ii :
    {x : ℕ × ℕ | let k := x.1; let n := x.2; 2 * k ≤ n ∧ deficiency n k > 1 ∧
      ∀ p, p.Prime → (p ∣ choose n k) → k < p}.Finite := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1094
docstring:
For all $n\ge 2k$ the least prime factor of $\binom{n}{k}$ is $\le\max(n/k,k)$, with only
finitely many exceptions.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1094 :
    {(n, k) : ℕ × ℕ | 0 < k ∧ 2 * k ≤ n ∧ (n.choose k).minFac > max (n / k) k}.Finite := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1095.variants.upper_conjecture
docstring: Ecklund, Erdős, and Selfridge [EES74] conjectured $g(k)\leq \exp((1+o(1))k)$.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1095.variants.upper_conjecture :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto f atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ ∀ᶠ k in atTop, g k ≤ exp (k * (1 + f k)) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1095.variants.lower_conjecture
docstring:
Erdős, Lacampagne, and Selfridge [ELS93] write 'it is clear to every right-thinking person' that
$g(k)\geq\exp(c\frac{k}{\log k})$ for some constant $c>0$.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1095.variants.lower_conjecture : ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ k in atTop, g k ≥ exp (c * k / log k) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1095.variants.log_equivalent
docstring: Sorenson, Sorenson, and Webster [SSWE20] give heuristic evidence that $\log g(k) \asymp \frac{k}{\log k}$.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1095.variants.log_equivalent : (fun k ↦ log (g k)) ~[atTop] (fun k ↦ k / log k) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_11
docstring: Is every odd $n > 1$ the sum of a squarefree number and a power of 2?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_11 (n : ℕ) (hn : Odd n) (hn' : 1 < n) :
    ∃ k l : ℕ, Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2 ^ l := by
  sorry

name: erdos_11.variants.not_four_dvd
docstring:
Erdős often asked this under the weaker assumption that $n > 1$
is not divisible by 4.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_11.variants.not_four_dvd (n : ℕ) (hn : ¬ 4 ∣ n) (hn' : 1 < n) :
    ∃ k l : ℕ , Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2^l := by
  sorry

name: erdos_11.variants.two_pow_two
docstring: Is every odd $n > 1$ the sum of a squarefree number and two powers of 2?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_11.variants.two_pow_two (n : ℕ) (hn : Odd n) (hn' : 1 < n) :
    ∃ k l m : ℕ , Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2^l + 2^m := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1101.parts.i
docstring: 1. There is NO good sequence with polynomial growth.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1101.parts.i :
    ¬ ∃ u, IsGood u ∧ ∃ k : ℕ, (fun n => (u n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n => (n : ℝ) ^ k) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1101.parts.ii
docstring: 2. There is a good sequence with sub-exponential growth.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1101.parts.ii :
    ∃ u, IsGood u ∧ (fun n => Real.log (u n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n => (n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1106.parts.i
docstring:
Let $p(n)$ be the partition number of $n$ and $F(n)$ be the number of distinct prime factors of
$∏_{i= 1} ^ {n} p(n)$, then $F(n)$ tends to infinity when $n$ tends to infinity.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1106.parts.i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ Tendsto (fun n => #(∏ i ∈ Icc 1 n, p i).primeFactors) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1106.parts.ii
docstring:
Let $p(n)$ be the partition number of $n$ and $F(n)$ be the number of distinct prime factors of
$∏_{i= 1} ^ {n} p(n)$, $F(n)>n$ for sufficiently large $n$.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1106.parts.ii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, #(∏ i ∈ Icc 1 n, p i).primeFactors > n := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1107
docstring: Let $r \ge 2$. Is every large integer the sum of at most $r + 1$ many $r$-powerful numbers?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1107 : ∀ r ≥ 2, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, SumOfRPowerful r n := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1108.parts.i
docstring: For each $k \geq 2$, does the set $A = \left\{ \sum_{n\in S}n! : S\subset \mathbb{N}\text{ finite}\right\}$ of all finite sums of distinct factorials contain only finitely many $k$-th powers?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1108.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 2,
    Set.Finite { a | a ∈ FactorialSums ∧ ∃ m : ℕ, m ^ k = a } := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1108.parts.ii
docstring: Does the set $A = \left\{ \sum_{n\in S}n! : S\subset \mathbb{N}\text{ finite}\right\}$ of all finite sums of distinct factorials contain only finitely many powerful numbers?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1108.parts.ii :
     answer(sorry) ↔ {a ∈ FactorialSums | IsPowerful a}.Finite := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1113
docstring:
**Erdős Problem 1113.** Do there exist Sierpiński numbers that possess no finite covering set
of primes?

Erdős and Graham [ErGr80] conjectured that the answer is yes. A negative answer would imply
that there are infinitely many Fermat primes.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1113 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ k, k.IsSierpinskiNumber ∧ ¬ HasFinitePrimeCoveringSet k := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1113.variants.filaseta_finch_kozek
docstring:
**Filaseta–Finch–Kozek conjecture (2008).** Every Sierpiński number is either a perfect power
or possesses a finite covering set of primes.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1113.variants.filaseta_finch_kozek :
    ∀ k, k.IsSierpinskiNumber →
      k.IsPerfectPower ∨ HasFinitePrimeCoveringSet k := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1133
docstring:
Let $C>0$. There exists $\epsilon>0$ such that if $n$ is sufficiently large the following holds.

For any $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in [-1,1]$ there exist $y_1,\ldots,y_n\in [-1,1]$ such that, if $P$ is a
polynomial of degree $m<(1+\epsilon)n$ with $P(x_i)=y_i$ for at least $(1-\epsilon)n$ many
$1\leq i\leq n$, then \[\max_{x\in [-1,1]}\lvert P(x)\rvert >C.\]
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 26 41]
theorem erdos_1133 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ C > (0 : ℝ), ∃ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ x : Fin n → Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1,
        ∃ y : Fin n → Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1,
          ∀ P : Polynomial ℝ,
            (P.natDegree : ℝ) < (1 + ε) * (n : ℝ) →
            ((Finset.univ.filter (fun i ↦ P.eval (x i : ℝ) = (y i : ℝ))).card : ℝ) ≥
              (1 - ε) * (n : ℝ) →
            ∃ z ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1, |P.eval z| > C := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1135
docstring:
The Collatz conjecture states that for any positive integer $n$, there exists a natural
number $m$ such that the $m$-th term of the sequence is 1.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11 37]
theorem erdos_1135 : type_of% CollatzConjecture.collatz_conjecture := by sorry

name: erdos_1137
docstring:
Let $d_n=p_{n+1}-p_n$, where $p_n$ denotes the $n$th prime. Is it true that
$$\frac{\max_{n < x}d_{n}d_{n-1}}{(\max_{n < x}d_n)^2}\to 0$$ as $x\to \infty$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1137 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
     Tendsto (fun x ↦
        (((range x).sup (fun n ↦ (primeGap n) * (primeGap (n - 1))) : ℕ) : ℝ) /
        (((range x).sup primeGap : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ 2) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1139
docstring:
Let $1\leq u_1 < u_2 < \cdots$ be the sequence of integers with at most $2$ prime factors.
Is it true that $$\limsup_{k \to \infty} \frac{u_{k+1}-u_k}{\log k}=\infty?$$
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1139 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      letI u := Nat.nth (fun n ↦ 0 < n ∧ Ω n ≤ 2)
      atTop.limsup (fun k : ℕ ↦ (((u (k + 1) : ℝ) - (u k : ℝ)) / Real.log (↑k + 1) : EReal)) = ⊤ := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1142
docstring:
Are there infinitely many $n > 2$ such that $n - 2^k$ is prime for all $k \geq 1$ with $2^k < n$?

The only known such $n$ are $4, 7, 15, 21, 45, 75, 105$ (OEIS [A039669](https://oeis.org/A039669)).
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1142 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ Infinite { n | Erdos1142Prop n } := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1145
docstring:
Let $A=\{1\leq a_1 < a_2 < \cdots\}$ and $B=\{1\leq b_1 < b_2 < \cdots\}$ be sets of integers with
$a_n/b_n\to 1$.

If $A+B$ contains all sufficiently large positive integers then is it true that
$\limsup 1_A\ast 1_B(n)=\infty$?

A conjecture of Erdős and Sárközy.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1145 : answer(sorry) ↔ Erdos1145Prop := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1146
docstring:
Is $B=\{2^m3^n : m,n\geq 0\}$ an essential component?

In [Ru99] Ruzsa states "The simplest set with a chance to be an essential component is the
collection of numbers in the form $2^m3^n$ and Erdős often asked whether it is an essential
component or not; I do not even have a plausible guess."
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1146 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ IsEssentialComponent { k | ∃ m n : ℕ, k = 2 ^ m * 3 ^ n } := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1150
docstring:
Is there some constant $c > 0$ such that, for all large enough $n$ and all polynomials $P$ of
degree $n$ with coefficients in $\{-1, 1\}$,
$$\max_{|z|=1} |P(z)| > (1 + c) \sqrt{n}?$$
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 12 30]
theorem erdos_1150 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop,
      ∀ P : ℂ[X],  (∀ i ≤ P.natDegree, P.coeff i = - 1 ∨ P.coeff i = 1) → P.natDegree = n →
        ⨆ z : Metric.sphere (0 : ℂ) 1, ‖P.eval (z : ℂ)‖ > (1 + c) * Real.sqrt n := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1167
docstring:
**Erdős Problem 1167.** Let $r \geq 2$ be finite, $\gamma \geq 2$, and $\lambda$ be an infinite
cardinal. Let $\kappa_\alpha$ be cardinals for all $\alpha < \gamma$. Is it true
that
$$2^\lambda \to (\kappa_\alpha + 1)_{\alpha < \gamma}^{r+1}$$
implies
$$\lambda \to (\kappa_\alpha)_{\alpha < \gamma}^r?$$
Here $+$ means cardinal addition, so that $\kappa_\alpha + 1 = \kappa_\alpha$
if $\kappa_\alpha$ is infinite.

A problem of Erdős, Hajnal, and Rado.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1167 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (r : ℕ), 2 ≤ r →
    ∀ (lam : Cardinal.{u}), ℵ₀ ≤ lam →
    ∀ (γ : Ordinal.{u}), 2 ≤ γ →
    ∀ (κ : γ.ToType → Cardinal.{u}),
      cardinalPartitionRel ((2 : Cardinal.{u}) ^ lam) (r + 1) γ (fun α => κ α + 1) →
      cardinalPartitionRel lam r γ κ := by
  sorry

name: finite_targets
docstring:
**Finite-target case.** When all $\kappa_\alpha$ are finite, $\kappa_\alpha + 1$
is the ordinary natural-number successor. Special case of `erdos_1167`.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem finite_targets (r : ℕ) (hr : 2 ≤ r) (lam : Cardinal.{u}) (hlam : ℵ₀ ≤ lam)
    (γ : Ordinal.{u}) (hγ : 2 ≤ γ) (n : γ.ToType → ℕ) :
    cardinalPartitionRel ((2 : Cardinal.{u}) ^ lam) (r + 1) γ
        (fun α => (n α : Cardinal.{u}) + 1) →
    cardinalPartitionRel lam r γ (fun α => (n α : Cardinal.{u})) := by
  sorry

name: binary_colors
docstring: **Binary-color case.** The $\gamma = 2$ specialization (two color classes).
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem binary_colors (r : ℕ) (hr : 2 ≤ r) (lam : Cardinal.{u}) (hlam : ℵ₀ ≤ lam)
    (κ : (2 : Ordinal.{u}).ToType → Cardinal.{u}) :
    cardinalPartitionRel ((2 : Cardinal.{u}) ^ lam) (r + 1) 2 (fun α => κ α + 1) →
    cardinalPartitionRel lam r 2 κ := by
  sorry

name: infinite_targets
docstring:
**Infinite-target case.** When all $\kappa_\alpha \geq \aleph_0$ are infinite and bounded by
$\lambda$, $\kappa_\alpha + 1 = \kappa_\alpha$, so the hypothesis simplifies to a "pure"
stepping-down lemma:
$$2^\lambda \to (\kappa_\alpha)_{\alpha<\gamma}^{r+1} \implies
   \lambda \to (\kappa_\alpha)_{\alpha<\gamma}^r.$$
The condition $\kappa_\alpha \leq \lambda$ is needed to avoid a size obstruction: without it, the
conclusion would require a subset of $\lambda$ of size $\kappa_\alpha > \lambda$, which is impossible
(see `infinite_targets_needs_bound`).
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem infinite_targets (r : ℕ) (hr : 2 ≤ r) (lam : Cardinal.{u}) (hlam : ℵ₀ ≤ lam)
    (γ : Ordinal.{u}) (hγ : 2 ≤ γ) (κ : γ.ToType → Cardinal.{u}) (hκ : ∀ i, ℵ₀ ≤ κ i)
    (hκ_le : ∀ i, κ i ≤ lam) :
    cardinalPartitionRel ((2 : Cardinal.{u}) ^ lam) (r + 1) γ κ →
    cardinalPartitionRel lam r γ κ := by
  sorry

name: r_eq_two
docstring:
**$r = 2$ case.** The stepping-down from 3-uniform to 2-uniform partition
relations: $2^\lambda \to (\kappa_\alpha + 1)_{\alpha<\gamma}^3$ implies
$\lambda \to (\kappa_\alpha)_{\alpha<\gamma}^2$. Generalises the classical
Erdős–Rado stepping-up/down theorem for pairs.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem r_eq_two (lam : Cardinal.{u}) (hlam : ℵ₀ ≤ lam)
    (γ : Ordinal.{u}) (hγ : 2 ≤ γ) (κ : γ.ToType → Cardinal.{u}) :
    cardinalPartitionRel ((2 : Cardinal.{u}) ^ lam) 3 γ (fun α => κ α + 1) →
    cardinalPartitionRel lam 2 γ κ := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1175
docstring:
Let $\kappa$ be an uncountable cardinal. Must there exist a cardinal $\lambda$ such that every
graph with chromatic number $\lambda$ contains a triangle-free subgraph with chromatic number
$\kappa$?

Shelah proved that a negative answer is consistent when
$\kappa = \lambda = \aleph_1$ (see `erdos_1175.variants.shelah_consistency`).
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1175 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (κ : Cardinal), ℵ₀ < κ →
      ∃ (μ : Cardinal),
        ∀ (V : Type*) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = μ →
          ∃ (H : G.Subgraph), H.coe.CliqueFree 3 ∧ H.coe.chromaticCardinal = κ := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1175.variants.threshold_formulation
docstring:
**Threshold reformulation variant.** Replaces `chromaticCardinal = λ` in the hypothesis
of `erdos_1175` with `λ ≤ chromaticCardinal` (a graph of chromatic number ≥ λ has a
triangle-free subgraph of chromatic number κ). This is a strengthening of `erdos_1175`
(see `erdos_1175.test.threshold_implies_exact`).
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1175.variants.threshold_formulation : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (κ : Cardinal), ℵ₀ < κ →
      ∃ (μ : Cardinal),
        ∀ (V : Type*) (G : SimpleGraph V), μ ≤ G.chromaticCardinal →
          ∃ (H : G.Subgraph), H.coe.CliqueFree 3 ∧ H.coe.chromaticCardinal = κ := by
  sorry

/- ## Sanity checks -/

name: erdos_1176
docstring:
Let $G$ be a graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$. Is it true that there is a colouring of the
edges with $\aleph_1$ many colours such that, in any countable colouring of the vertices, there
exists a vertex colour containing all edge colours?

A problem of Erdős, Galvin, and Hajnal. The consistency of this was proved by Hajnal and Komjáth.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 3 5]
theorem erdos_1176 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = aleph 1 →
      ∃ (EColor : Type) (_ : mk EColor = aleph 1) (c_edge : G.edgeSet → EColor),
        ∀ (VColor : Type) (_ : mk VColor ≤ aleph 0) (c_vert : V → VColor),
          ∃ (vc : VColor),
            ∀ (ec : EColor), ∃ (u v : V) (h : G.Adj u v),
              c_vert u = vc ∧ c_vert v = vc ∧ c_edge ⟨s(u, v), h⟩ = ec := by
  sorry

name: erdos_119.parts.iii
docstring:
Question 3:

Is it true that there exists $c > 0$ such that, for all large $n$, $\sum_{k \leq n} M_k > n^{1 + c}$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 30]
theorem erdos_119.parts.iii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (z : ℕ → ℂ) (hz : ∀ i : ℕ, ‖z i‖ = 1),
      ∃ (c : ℝ) (hc : c > 0), ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
        ∑ k ∈ range n, M z k > n ^ (1 + c) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1192
docstring:
Does there exist, for all $r\geq 2$, a basis $A$ of order $r$ (so that $f_r(n)>0$ for all
large $n$) such that $$\sum_{n\leq x}f_r(n)^2 \ll x$$ for all $x$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1192 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ r ≥ 2, ∃ A : Set ℕ,
        (∀ᶠ n in atTop, f_r A r n > 0) ∧
        (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ ∑ n ∈ range (x + 1), (f_r A r n : ℝ) ^ 2) =O[atTop]
          (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ (x : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1199
docstring:
Is it true that in any 2-colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ there exists an infinite set $A$
such that all elements of $A+A$ are the same colour?

A conjecture of Owings [Ow74].
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1199 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (color : ℕ → Fin 2), ∃ (A : Set ℕ),
    A.Infinite ∧ ∀ n ∈ (A+A), ∀ m ∈ (A+A), color n = color m := by 
  sorry

name: erdos_12.parts.iii
docstring:
Let $A$ be an infinite set such that there are no distinct $a,b,c \in A$
such that $a \mid (b+c)$ and $b,c > a$. Is it true that $∑_{n \in A} \frac{1}{n} < \infty$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_12.parts.iii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), IsGood A → Summable (fun (n : A) ↦ (1 / n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_120
docstring:
Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be an infinite set. Must there be a set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}$
of positive measure which does not contain any set of the shape $a * A + b$
for some $a,b \in \mathbb{R}$ and $a \neq 0$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5 28]
theorem erdos_120 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ A : Set ℝ, A.Infinite → Erdos120For A := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1201
docstring:
Is it true that for every $\epsilon,\eta>0$ there exists a $k$ such that the density of $n$
for which $P(n(n+1)\cdots(n+k))>n^{1-\epsilon}$ is at least $1-\eta$ (where $P(m)$ is the greatest
prime divisor of $m$)?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1201 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ ε > 0, ∀ η > 0, ∃ k : ℕ,
        atTop.liminf (fun x : ℕ ↦
          (((count (Erdos1201Set ε k) x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ)) : EReal)) ≥ (1 - η : EReal) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1203
docstring: Prove that $F(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1203 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ Tendsto F atTop atTop := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1209.parts.iii.b
docstring: Are there $n$ such that $n+2^{2^k}$ is always squarefree?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1209.parts.iii.b :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ k : ℕ, Squarefree (n + 2 ^ (2 ^ k)) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1209.parts.iii.c
docstring: Are there $n$ such that $n+2^{2^k}$ is infinitely often a prime?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1209.parts.iii.c :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ n : ℕ, {k | (n + 2 ^ (2 ^ k)).Prime}.Infinite := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1209.parts.iii.d
docstring: Are there $n$ such that $n+2^{2^k}$ is infinitely often squarefree?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1209.parts.iii.d :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ n : ℕ, {k | Squarefree (n + 2 ^ (2 ^ k))}.Infinite := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1210
docstring:
Let $A\subseteq [1,n)$ be a set of integers such that $(a,b)=1$ for all distinct $a,b\in A$.
Is it true that $\sum_{a\in A}\frac{1}{n-a}\leq \sum_{p < n}\frac{1}{p}+O(1)$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1210 :
  answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ A : Finset ℕ,
      (∀ a ∈ A, 1 ≤ a ∧ a < n) →
      (∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ A, a ≠ b → a.Coprime b) →
      ∑ a ∈ A, (1 / ((n : ℝ) - a)) ≤ (∑ p ∈ (range n).filter Prime, (1 / (p : ℝ))) + C := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1210.variants.er80_correction
docstring:
In [Er80] he claims he "did not state this quite correctly" in [Er77c]. The problem in [Er77c] which
Erdős is presumably referring to states that if $n < q_1 < \cdots < q_k\leq m$ is the set of primes
in $(n,m]$ then $\sum \frac{1}{q_i-n} < \sum_{p < m-n}\frac{1}{p}+O(1)$.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1210.variants.er80_correction :
  answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n m : ℕ, n < m →
      ∑ q ∈ (Ioc n m).filter Prime, (1 / ((q : ℝ) - n)) <
      (∑ p ∈ (range (m - n)).filter Prime, (1 / (p : ℝ))) + C := by
  sorry

name: erdos_1212
docstring:
Let $G$ be the graph with vertex set those pairs $(x,y)\in \mathbb{N}^2$ with
$\mathrm{gcd}(x,y)=1$, in which we join two vertices if the differ in only one coordinate, and
there by $\pm 1$.

Is there a path going to infinity on $G$, say $P$, such that for all $(x,y)\in P$ both
$\min(x,y)>1$ and at least one of $x$ or $y$ is composite?

The weaker version (only $\min(x,y) > 1$) was solved by C. Stewart via the prime-pair path
$(p_k, p_{k+1}) \to (p_{k+1}, p_{k+2})$, as recounted in [Er80]; the compositeness condition
forbids those anchors and the question is open.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1212 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ × ℕ, Function.Injective f ∧ (∀ n, Adj (f n) (f (n + 1))) ∧
      (∀ n, Valid (f n)) ∧
      Tendsto (fun n => (f n).1 + (f n).2) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/- ### Verified partial results (2026): machine-checked cores -/

name: erdos_123
docstring:
**Erdős Problem #123**

Let $a, b, c$ be three integers which are pairwise coprime. Is every large integer
the sum of distinct integers of the form $a^k b^l c^m$ ($k, l, m ≥ 0$), none of which
divide any other?

Equivalently: is the set $\{a^k b^l c^m : k, l, m \geq 0\}$ d-complete?

Note: For this not to reduce to the two-integer case, we need the integers
to be greater than one and distinct.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_123 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ a > 1, ∀ b > 1, ∀ c > 1, PairwiseCoprime a b c →
    IsDComplete (↑(powers a) * ↑(powers b) * ↑(powers c)) := by sorry

name: erdos_123.variants.powers_2_3_5_snug
docstring:
A stronger conjecture for numbers of the form $2^k 3^l 5^j$.

For any $ε > 0$, all large integers $n$ can be written as the sum of distinct integers
$b_1 < ... < b_t$ of the form $2^k 3^l 5^j$ where $b_t < (1 + ϵ) b_1$.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_123.variants.powers_2_3_5_snug :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      ∃ A : Finset ℕ, (A : Set ℕ) ⊆ ↑(powers 2) * ↑(powers 3) * ↑(powers 5) ∧ IsSnug ε A ∧
        ∑ x ∈ A, x = n := by sorry

name: erdos124.ne_zero
docstring:
Let $k \ne 0$ and $3\leq d_1 < d_2 < \cdots < d_r$ be integers of gcd equal to $1$ such that
$$\sum_{1 \le i \le r}\frac 1{d_i - 1} \ge 1.$$
Can all sufficiently large integers be written as a sum of the shape $\sum_i c_ia_i$
where $c_i \in \{0, 1\}$ and $a_i$ is divisible by $d_i ^ k$ and has only the digits $0, 1$ when
written in base $d_i$?

Conjectured by Burr, Erdős, Graham, and Li [BEGL96]
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
lemma erdos124.ne_zero : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ k ≠ 0, ∀ D : Finset ℕ, (∀ d ∈ D, 3 ≤ d) → 1 ≤ ∑ d ∈ D, (d - 1 : ℚ)⁻¹ → D.gcd id = 1 →
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, n ∈ ∑ d ∈ D, sumsOfDistinctPowers d k := by
  sorry

name: erdos_125.variants.positive_upper_density
docstring:
Literature question:
Does $A + B$ have positive upper density?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_125.variants.positive_upper_density :
    answer(sorry) ↔ 0 < (A + B).upperDensity := by
  sorry

name: erdos_125.variants.zero_density
docstring:
Case 1:
Does $A + B$ have zero upper and lower density?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_125.variants.zero_density :
    answer(sorry) ↔ (A + B).upperDensity = 0 ∧ (A + B).lowerDensity = 0 := by
  sorry

name: erdos_125.variants.zero_lower_positive_upper_density
docstring:
Case 2:
Does $A + B$ have zero lower density, but positive upper density?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_125.variants.zero_lower_positive_upper_density :
    answer(sorry) ↔ (A + B).lowerDensity = 0 ∧ 0 < (A + B).upperDensity := by
  sorry

name: erdos_126
docstring:
Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that if $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ has $|A| = n$ then
$\prod_{a\neq b\in A}(a + b)$ has at least $f(n)$ distinct prime factors.
Is it true that $\frac{f(n)}{\log n} \to\infty$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_126 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (f : ℕ → ℕ), IsMaximalAddFactorsCard f →
    Tendsto (fun n => f n / Real.log n) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

name: erdos_126.variants.isLittleO
docstring: Erdős says that $f(n) = o(\frac{n}{\log n})$ has never been proved.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_126.variants.isLittleO
    (f : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hf : IsMaximalAddFactorsCard f) :
    (fun (n : ℕ) => (f n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun (n : ℕ) => n / Real.log n) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_128
docstring:
Let G be a graph with n vertices such that every subgraph on ≥ $n/2$
vertices has more than $n^2/50$ edges. Must G contain a triangle?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_128 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (V' : Set V),
      2 * V'.ncard + 1 ≥ Fintype.card V →
        50 * (G.induce V').edgeSet.ncard > Fintype.card V ^ 2 → ¬ G.CliqueFree 3 := by
  sorry

name: erdos_13.variants.general
docstring:
A general version asks, for a fixed $r \in \mathbb{N}$, if a set
$A \subseteq \{1, ..., N\}$ has no $a \in A$ and $b_1, ..., b_r \in A$ such that
$a | (b_1 + ... + b_r)$ and $a < \min(b_1, ..., b_r)$, then is it true that
$|A| \le N/(r+1) + O(1)$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_13.variants.general : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ r : ℕ, ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ N : ℕ,
    ∀ A ⊆ Icc 1 N,
    (∀ a ∈ A, ∀ (b : Fin r → ℕ), (∀ i, b i ∈ A) → (∀ i, a < b i) →
      ¬ (a ∣ ∑ i, b i)) →
    (A.card : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) / (r + 1) + C := by
  sorry

name: erdos_137
docstring:
Let $k\geq 3$. Can the product of any $k$ consecutive integers $N$ ever be powerful? That is,
must there always exist a prime $p\mid N$ such that $p^2\nmid N$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_137 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 3, ∀ n, ¬ (∏ x ∈ Finset.Ioc n (n + k), x).Powerful := by
  sorry

name: erdos_137.variants.multiple_powerful_factors
docstring:
Erdős [Er82c] conjectures that, if $k$ is fixed, then for all $n$ sufficiently large and all
positive integers $m$, there must be at least $k$ distinct primes $p$ such that
$p\mid m(m+1)\cdots (m+n)$ and yet $p^2$ does not divide the right hand side.

[Er82c] Erdős, Paul, "Miscellaneous problems in number theory". Congr. Numer. (1982), 25-45.,
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_137.variants.multiple_powerful_factors (k : ℕ) : ∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop,
    ∀ (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m),
    letI N := ∏ x ∈ Finset.Ioc m (m + n), x
    ∃ P : Finset ℕ, P.card = k ∧ ∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime ∧
    p ∣ N ∧ ¬ p ^ 2 ∣ N := by
  sorry

name: erdos_138
docstring:
In [Er80] Erdős asks whether
$$ \lim_{k \to \infty} (W(k))^{1/k} = \infty $$
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_138 : answer(sorry) ↔ atTop.Tendsto (fun k => (W k : ℝ)^(1/(k : ℝ))) atTop := by
  sorry

name: erdos_138.variants.quotient
docstring: In [Er81] Erdős asks whether $\frac{W(k+1)}{W(k)} \to \infty$.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_138.variants.quotient :
    answer(sorry) ↔ atTop.Tendsto (fun k => ((W (k + 1) : ℚ)/(W k))) atTop := by
  sorry

name: erdos_138.variants.dvd_two_pow
docstring: In [Er80] Erdős asks whether $W(k)/2^k\to \infty$.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_138.variants.dvd_two_pow :
    answer(sorry) ↔ atTop.Tendsto (fun k => ((W k : ℚ)/ (2 ^ k))) atTop := by
  sorry

name: erdos_14.parts.i
docstring:
Let $A ⊆ \mathbb{N}$. Let $B ⊆ \mathbb{N}$ be the set of integers which are representable
in exactly one way as the sum of two elements from $A$. Is it true that for all
$\epsilon > 0$ and large $N$, $|\{1,\ldots,N\} \setminus B| \gg_\epsilon N^{1/2 - \epsilon}$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_14.parts.i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ A, ∀ ε > 0, nonUniqueSumCount A ≫ almostSquareRoot ε := by sorry

name: erdos_14.parts.ii
docstring: Is it possible that $|\{1,\ldots,N\} \setminus B| = o(N^\frac{1}{2})$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_14.parts.ii :

name: erdos_193
docstring:
Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^3$ be a finite set and let $A = \lbrace a_1, a_2, \ldots \rbrace$ be
an infinite $S$-walk, so that $a_{i+1} - a_i \in S$ for all $i$. Must $A$ contain three collinear
points?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_193 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ S : Set (Fin 3 → ℤ), S.Finite →
      /- The statement's $A = \lbrace a_1, a_2, \ldots \rbrace$ is an infinite set.

      If the sequence only takes finitely many values, one value has to repeat infinitely many
      times, which would yield a trivial collinear triple (x, x, x). In this case, the conjecture
      would hold for degenerate S-walks. Another case is constant S-walks, which would render the
      conjecture trivially false (finite loop ranges have no 3 distinct points).

      Assuming the authors intend to stay away from these degenerate cases, we formalize this by
      requiring an infinite range (and require distinct points). -/
      ∀ a : ℕ → Fin 3 → ℤ, IsSWalk S a → (range a).Infinite →
      HasCollinearTriple ℚ (range (fun n ↦ (↑) ∘ a n : ℕ → Fin 3 → ℚ)) := by
  sorry

theorem erdos_241.variants.generalization (r : ℕ) (hr : r ≥ 2) :  BoseChowlaConjecture r := by
  sorry

name: erdos_242
docstring:
For every $n>2$ there exist distinct integers $1 ≤ x < y < z$
such that $\frac 4 n = \frac 1 x + \frac 1 y + \frac 1 z$.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_242 (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 < n) :
    ∃ x y z : ℕ, 1 ≤ x ∧ x < y ∧ y < z ∧
      (4 / n : ℚ) = 1 / x + 1 / y + 1 / z := by
  sorry

name: erdos_242.variants.schinzel_generalization
docstring:
Schinzel conjectured (see [Si56]) the generalisation that, for any fixed $a$, if $n$ is sufficiently
large in terms of $a$ then there exist distinct integers $1\leq x < y < z$ such that
$\frac{a}{n} = \frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{y}+\frac{1}{z}.$
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_242.variants.schinzel_generalization
    (a : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) :
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ x y z : ℕ, 1 ≤ x ∧ x < y ∧ y < z ∧
      (a / n : ℚ) = 1 / x + 1 / y + 1 / z := by
  sorry

name: erdos_243
docstring:
Let $a_1 < a_2 < \dots$ be a sequence of integers such that
$\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{a_n}{a_{n-1}^2} = 1$ and $\sum \frac{1}{a_n} \in \mathbb{Q}$.

Then, for all sufficiently large $n \ge 1$, $a_n = a_{n-1}^2 - a_{n-1} + 1$.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 40]
theorem erdos_243 (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha₀ : StrictMono a)
    (ha₁ : Tendsto (fun n ↦ (a n : ℝ) / a (n - 1) ^ 2) atTop (𝓝 1))
    (ha₂ : Summable ((1 : ℚ) / a ·)) :
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, a n = a (n - 1) ^ 2 - a (n - 1) + 1 := by
  sorry

name: erdos_244
docstring:
Let $C > 1$. Does the set of integers of the form $p + \lfloor C^k \rfloor$,
for some prime $p$ and $k\geq 0$, have density $>0$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_244 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ C > (1 : ℝ), 0 < { p + ⌊C ^ k⌋₊ | (p) (k) (_ : p.Prime) }.lowerDensity := by
  sorry

name: erdos_247
docstring:
Let $n_1 < n_2 < \cdots$ be a sequence of integers such that
$$
  \limsup \frac{n_k}{k} = \infty.
$$
Is
$$
  \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{2^{n_k}}
$$
transcendental?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_247 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (n : ℕ → ℕ), (StrictMono n) →
    atTop.limsup (fun k => (n k / k.succ : EReal)) = ⊤ →
    Transcendental ℚ (∑' k, (1 : ℝ) / 2 ^ n k) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_249
docstring:
Is
$$\sum_{n} \frac{\phi(n)}{2^n}$$
irrational? Here $\phi$ is the Euler totient function.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_249 : answer(sorry) ↔ Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (φ n) / (2 ^ n)) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_25
docstring:
Let $n_1 < n_2 < \dots$ be an arbitrary sequence of integers, each with an associated residue class
$a_i \pmod{n_i}$. Let $A$ be the set of integers $n$ such that for every $i$ either $n < n_i$ or
$n \not\equiv a_i \pmod{n_i}$. Must the logarithmic density of $A$ exist?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_25 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (seq_n : ℕ → ℕ) (seq_a : ℕ → ℤ), (∀ i, 0 < seq_n i) → StrictMono seq_n →
      ∃ d, Set.HasLogDensity
        { x : ℕ | ∀ i, (x : ℤ) < seq_n i ∨ ¬((x : ℤ) ≡ seq_a i [ZMOD seq_n i]) } d := by
  sorry

name: erdos_251
docstring: Is $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{p_n}{2^n}$ irrational? Here $p_n$ is the $n$-th prime ($p_1=2, p_2=3, \dots$).
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_251 : answer(sorry) ↔ Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.nth Nat.Prime n) / (2 ^ n)) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_252
docstring: Erdős Problem 252: irrationality of the sum for a given $k$.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_252 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 1, Irrational (erdos_252_sum k) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_252.variants.k_ge_five
docstring: For a fixed `k ≥ 5`, is `∑ σ k n / n!` irrational?.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_252.variants.k_ge_five :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 5, Irrational (erdos_252_sum k) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_254
docstring:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be such that $\lvert A\cap [1,2x]\rvert -\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert \to
\infty\textrm{ as }x\to \infty$ and $\sum_{n\in A} \{ \theta n\}=\infty$ for every $\theta\in
(0,1)$, where $\{x\}$ is the distance of $x$ from the nearest integer. Then every sufficiently large
integer is the sum of distinct elements of $A$.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_254 :
    ∀ (A : Set ℕ),
      (Tendsto (fun x : ℕ ↦ (A ∩ Icc 1 (2 * x)).ncard - (A ∩ Icc 1 x).ncard) atTop atTop) ∧
      (∀ θ : ℝ, 0 < θ → θ < 1 → ¬ Summable (fun n : A ↦ distToNearestInt (θ * (n : ℝ)))) →
        ∀ᶠ m in atTop, IsSumOfDistinct A m := by
  sorry

name: erdos_257
docstring:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set. Is
$$
\sum_{n\in A} \frac{1}{2^n - 1}
$$
irrational?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_257 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A.Infinite →
    Irrational (∑' n : A, (1 : ℝ) / (2 ^ n.1 - 1)) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_260
docstring:
Let $a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ be an increasing sequence such that $\frac{a_n}{n} \to \infty$.
Is the sum $\sum_{n}^{\infty} \frac{a_n}{2^{a_n}}$ irrational?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_260 : answer(sorry) ↔
                  ∀ a : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ s : ℝ,
                  StrictMono a →
                  Tendsto (fun n => (a n : ℝ ) / n ) atTop atTop →
                  HasSum (fun n => (a n : ℝ ) / 2 ^ a n) s → Irrational s :=
  sorry

-- TODO: Add a proof of the theorem under the strong assumption $a_{n+1}-a_n → \infty$
-- TODO: Add a proof of the theorem under the strong assumption $a_n \gg n\sqrt{\log{n}\log{\log{n}}}$

name: erdos_263.parts.i
docstring: Is $a_n = 2^{2^n}$ an irrationality sequence in the above sense?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_263.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ IsIrrationalitySequence (fun n : ℕ => 2 ^ 2 ^ n) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_264.parts.ii
docstring: Is $n!$ an example of an irrationality sequence?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_264.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ IsIrrationalitySequence Nat.factorial := by sorry

name: erdos_267
docstring:
Let $F_1=F_2=1$ and $F_{n+1} = F_n + F_{n-1}$ be the Fibonacci sequence.
Let $n_1 < n_2 < \dots$ be an infinite sequence with $\frac{n_{k+1}}{n_k} \ge c > 1$. Must
$\sum_k \frac 1 {F_{n_k}}$ be irrational?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_267 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (n : ℕ → ℕ) (c > (1 : ℚ)), StrictMono n → (∀ k, c ≤ n (k+1) / n k) →
    Irrational (∑' k, 1 / (Nat.fib <| n k)) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_267.variants.generalisation_ratio_limit_to_infinity
docstring:
Let $F_1=F_2=1$ and $F_{n+1} = F_n + F_{n-1}$ be the Fibonacci sequence.
Let $n_1 < n_2 < \dots$ be an infinite sequence with $\frac {n_k}{k} \to \infty$. Must
$\sum_k \frac 1 {F_{n_k}}$ be irrational?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_267.variants.generalisation_ratio_limit_to_infinity : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (n : ℕ → ℕ),
    StrictMono n → Filter.Tendsto (fun k => (n (k+1) / k.succ : ℝ)) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop →
    Irrational (∑' k, 1 / (Nat.fib <| n k)) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_269.variants.rational
docstring:
Let $P$ be a finite set of primes with $|P| \ge 2$ and let
$\{a_1 < a_2 < \dots\}$ be the set of positive integers whose prime factors
are all in $P$. Is the sum
$$ \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{[a_1,\ldots,a_n]} $$
rational?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_269.variants.rational : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ᵉ (P : Finset ℕ) (h : ∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) (h_card : P.card ≥ 2),
    ∃ (q : ℚ), q = (series (P : Set ℕ)) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_269.variants.irrational
docstring:
Let $P$ be a finite set of primes with $|P| \ge 2$ and let
$\{a_1 < a_2 < \dots\}$ be the set of positive integers whose prime factors
are all in $P$. Is the sum
$$ \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{[a_1,\ldots,a_n]} $$
irrational?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_269.variants.irrational : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ᵉ (P : Finset ℕ) (h : ∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) (h_card : P.card ≥ 2),
    Irrational (series (P : Set ℕ)) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_272
docstring:
Let $N\geq 1$. What is the largest $t$ such that there are
$A_1,\ldots,A_t\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $A_i\cap A_j$ a non-empty
arithmetic progression for all $i\neq j$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_272 :
    (fun N ↦ (maxArithInterCard N : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_272.variants.szabo_strong
docstring:
Szabo asks whether the maximal $t$ is given by
$$
  \frac{N^2}{2} + O(N)
$$
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_272.variants.szabo_strong :
    (fun N ↦ (maxArithInterCard N - N ^ 2 / 2 : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun N : ℕ ↦ (N : ℝ) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_273
docstring: Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are of the form $p-1$ for some primes $p \geq 5$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_273 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ, ∀ i, ∃ (p : ℕ), p.Prime ∧ 5 ≤ p ∧
    c.moduli i = Ideal.span {↑(p - 1)} := by
  sorry

name: erdos_274
docstring:
If $G$ is a group, can there exist an exact covering of $G$ by more than one coset
of different sizes? (i.e. each element is contained in exactly one of the cosets.)

The conjectured answer is no: in every such exact covering, two of the subgroups have
the same cardinality.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem erdos_274 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type*) [Group G],
    1 < ENat.card G → ∀ (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι],
    ∀ (P : Group.ExactCovering G ι), 1 < Fintype.card ι →
    ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ #(P.parts i) = #(P.parts j) := by
  sorry

name: herzog_schonheim
docstring:
Let $G$ be a group, and let $A = \{a_1G_1, \dots, a_kG_k\}$ be a finite system of left cosets of
subgroups $G_1, \dots, G_k$ of $G$.

Herzog and Schönheim conjectured that if $A$ forms a partition of $G$ with $k > 1$, then the
indices $[G:G_1], \dots, [G:G_k]$ cannot be distinct.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem herzog_schonheim {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : 1 < ENat.card G) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (hι : 1 < Fintype.card ι) (P : Group.ExactCovering G ι) :
    ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ (P.parts i).index = (P.parts j).index := by
  sorry

name: erdos_276
docstring:
Is there an infinite Lucas sequence $a_0, a_1, \ldots$ where $a_{n+2} = a_{n+1} + a_n$ for
$n \ge 0$ such that all $a_k$ are composite, and yet no integer has a common factor with every
term of the sequence?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_276 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
    IsLucasSequence a ∧ (∀ k, (a k).Composite) ∧ (∀ n > 1, ∃ k, Nat.gcd n (a k) = 1) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_279
docstring:
Let $k\geq 3$. Is there a choice of congruence classes $a_p\pmod{p}$ for every prime $p$
such that all sufficiently large integers can be written as $a_p+tp$ for some prime $p$
and integer $t\geq k$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_279 :  answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k : Nat, k ≥ 3 →
    ∃ a : Nat → Nat, ∃ N : Nat, (∀ p : Nat, p.Prime → a p < p) ∧
    ∀ n ≥ N, ∃ p : Nat, ∃ t ≥ k, p.Prime ∧ n = a p + t * p := by
  sorry

name: erdos_28
docstring:
If $A ⊆ \mathbb{N}$ is such that $A + A$ contains all but finitely many integers then
 $\limsup 1_A ∗ 1_A(n) = \infty$.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_28 (A : Set ℕ) (h : (A + A)ᶜ.Finite) :
    limsup (fun (n : ℕ) => (sumRep A n : ℕ∞)) atTop = (⊤ : ℕ∞) := by
  sorry

-- TODO(firsching): add the theorems/conjectures for the comments on the page

name: erdos_282
docstring:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set and consider the following
greedy algorithm for a rational $x\in (0,1)$: choose the minimal $n\in A$ such
that $n\geq 1/x$ and repeat with $x$ replaced by $x-\frac{1}{n}$. If this
terminates after finitely many steps then this produces a representation of
$x$ as the sum of distinct unit fractions with denominators from $A$.

Does this process always terminate if $x$ has odd denominator and $A$ is the
set of odd numbers?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_282 {x : ℚ} (hx : x ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1) (hx_den : Odd x.den) :
    greedyUnitFractionRem { n | Odd n } x =ᶠ[atTop] 0 := by
  sorry

name: erdos_282.variants.general
docstring: More generally, for which pairs $x$ and $A$ does this process terminate?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_282.variants.general (x : ℚ) (A : Set ℕ) :
      greedyUnitFractionRem A x =ᶠ[atTop] 0 ↔ (x, A) ∈ (answer(sorry) : Set (ℚ × Set ℕ)) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_282.variants.graham
docstring:
Graham has shown that $\frac{m}{n}$ is the sum of distinct unit fractions
with denominators $\equiv a\pmod{d}$ if and only if
$$\left(\frac{n}{(n,a,d)},\frac{d}{(a,d)}\right)=1.$$
Does the greedy algorithm always
terminate in such cases?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_282.variants.graham {x : ℚ} (hx : x ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1) {a d : ℕ} (hd : 1 < d)
    (h : (x.den / x.den.gcd (a.gcd d)).gcd (d / a.gcd d) = 1) :
    (greedyUnitFractionRem { n | n ≡ a [MOD d] } x =ᶠ[atTop] 0) ↔ answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_282.variants.sq
docstring:
Graham has also shown that $x$ is the sum of distinct unit fractions with
square denominators if and only if $x\in [0,\pi^2/6-1)\cup [1,\pi^2/6)$. Does the
greedy algorithm for this always terminate? Erdős and Graham believe not - indeed, perhaps it
fails to terminate almost always.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_282.variants.sq :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ x : ℚ, (x : ℝ) ∈ Set.Ico 0 (π ^ 2 / 6 - 1) ∪ Set.Ico 1 (π ^ 2 / 6) →
      greedyUnitFractionRem { n | IsSquare n } x =ᶠ[atTop] 0 := by
  sorry

name: erdos_287
docstring:
Let $k\geq2$. Is it true that, for any distinct integers
$1 < n_1 < \cdots < n_k$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^k \frac{1}{n_i} = 1$,
we must have $\max(n_{i+1} - n_i) \geq 3$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_287 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (s : Fin k → ℕ),
    StrictMono s → 1 < s ⟨0, by omega⟩ →
    ∑ i : Fin k, 1/ (s i : ℝ) = 1 →
    3 ≤ max_gap k s:= by
  sorry

name: erdos_287.variants.prime_conjecture
docstring:
For all large $N$, there exists a prime $p \in [N, 2N]$ such that $\frac{p+1}{2}$ is also prime.

This is an open conjecture. If true, it would imply `erdos_287` for all but at most finitely
many exceptions (see `erdos_287.variants.prime_conjecture_implies`).
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_287.variants.prime_conjecture : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ N₀ : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N₀ ≤ N →
      ∃ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p ∧ N ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 2 * N ∧ Nat.Prime ((p + 1) / 2) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_288
docstring:
Is it true that there are only finitely many pairs of intervals $I_1$, $I_2$ such that
$$
\sum_{n_1 \in I_1} \frac{1}{n_1} + \sum_{n_2 \in I_2} \frac{1}{n_2} \in \mathbb{N}?
$$
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_288 : answer(sorry) ↔ Set.Finite { I : Fin 2 → ℕ+ × ℕ+ |
    ∀ j, (I j).1 ≤ (I j).2 ∧
      ∃ n : ℕ+, (∑ j : Fin 2, ∑ nⱼ ∈ Set.Icc (I j).1 (I j).2, (nⱼ⁻¹ : ℚ)) = n } := by
  sorry

name: erdos_288.variants.i2_card_eq_1
docstring: This is still open even if $|I_2| = 1$.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_288.variants.i2_card_eq_1 : answer(sorry) ↔ Set.Finite { (I, n₂) : (ℕ+ × ℕ+) × ℕ+ |
    I.1 ≤ I.2 ∧ ∃ n : ℕ+, ∑ n₁ ∈ Set.Icc I.1 I.2, (n₁⁻¹ : ℚ) + (n₂⁻¹ : ℚ) = n } := by
  sorry

name: erdos_288.variants.k_intervals
docstring: It is perhaps true with two intervals replaced by any $k$ intervals.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_288.variants.k_intervals : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k, Set.Finite { I : Fin k → ℕ+ × ℕ+ |
    ∀ j, (I j).1 ≤ (I j).2 ∧
      ∃ n : ℕ+, (∑ j : Fin k, ∑ nⱼ ∈ Set.Icc (I j).1 (I j).2, (nⱼ⁻¹ : ℚ)) = n } := by
  sorry

name: erdos_288.variants.exists_k_gt_2
docstring: Is it true for any $k > 2$ that only finitely many $k$ intervals satisfy this condition?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_288.variants.exists_k_gt_2 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ k > 2, Set.Finite { I : Fin k → ℕ+ × ℕ+ |
      ∀ j, (I j).1 ≤ (I j).2 ∧
        ∃ n : ℕ+, (∑ j : Fin k, ∑ nⱼ ∈ Set.Icc (I j).1 (I j).2, (nⱼ⁻¹ : ℚ)) = n } := by
  sorry

name: erdos_289
docstring:
Is it true that, for all sufficiently large $k$, there exists finite intervals
$I_1, \dotsc, I_k \subset \mathbb{N}$ with $|I_i| \geq 2$ for $1 \leq i \leq k$ such that
$$
1 = \sum_{i=1}^k \sum_{n \in I_i} \frac{1}{n}.
$$
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_289 : answer(sorry) ↔
    (∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, ∃ I : Fin k → ℕ × ℕ,
    (∀ i, (I i).1 < (I i).2) ∧
    (∀ i j, i ≠ j → (I i).2 < (I j).1 ∨ (I j).2 < (I i).1) ∧
    ∑ i, ∑ n ∈ .Icc (I i).1 (I i).2, (n⁻¹ : ℚ) = 1) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_291.parts.i
docstring:
Let $n\geq 1$ and define $L_n$ to be the least common multiple of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $a_n$ by
$\sum_{1\leq k\leq n}\frac{1}{k}=\frac{a_n}{L_n}$.

Is it true that $(a_n,L_n)=1$ occurs for infinitely many $n$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_291.parts.i :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      { n : ℕ | Nat.gcd (a n) (L n) = 1 }.Infinite := by
  sorry

name: erdos_291.variants.shiu_heuristic_asymptotic
docstring:
This leads to a heuristic prediction (see for example a preprint of Shiu [Sh16]) of
$\asymp\frac{x}{\log x}$ for the number of $n\in [1,x]$ such that $(a_n,L_n)=1$.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_291.variants.shiu_heuristic_asymptotic :
    Asymptotics.IsTheta atTop
      (fun x : ℕ ↦ ((((Finset.Icc 1 x).filter (fun n ↦ Nat.gcd (a n) (L n) = 1)).card : ℝ)))
      (fun x : ℕ ↦ (x : ℝ) / Real.log x) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_291.variants.shiu_heuristic_density_zero
docstring:
In particular, there should be infinitely many $n$, but the set of such $n$ should have
density zero. Unfortunately this heuristic is difficult to turn into a proof.
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_291.variants.shiu_heuristic_density_zero :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦
      ((((Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (fun n ↦ Nat.gcd (a n) (L n) = 1)).card : ℝ) / (N : ℝ)))
      atTop (nhds 0) := by
  sorry

name: erdos_295
docstring:
Let $k(N)$ denote the smallest $k$ such that there exists
$N ≤ n_1 < ⋯ < n_k$ with $\frac 1 {n_1} + ... + \frac 1 {n_k} = 1$

Is it true that $\lim_{N \to \infty} k(N) - (e - 1)N = \infty$?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_295 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ Filter.atTop.Tendsto (fun N => k N - (rexp 1 - 1)*N) Filter.atTop := by
  sorry

name: erdos_3
docstring:
If $A \subset \mathbb{N} has $\sum_{n \in A}\frac 1 n = \infty$, then must $A$ contain arbitrarily
long arithmetic progressions?
statement:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_3 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ A : Set ℕ,
    (¬ Summable fun a : A ↦ 1 / (a : ℝ)) →
    ∃ᶠ (k : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ S ⊆ A, S.IsAPOfLength k := by
  sorry
